import unittest
from gateway import handle
from workload import equivalent


class Examples(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_example_1(self):
        request = {'layer': 4,
 'packets': [{'k': [[0]], 'q': [[0], [0]], 'v': [[1]]},
             {'k': [[0]], 'q': [[0], [0]], 'v': [[3]]},
             {'k': [[0]], 'q': [[0], [0]], 'v': [[11]]}],
 'window': 2}
        expected = {'contexts': [[[1], [1]], [[2], [2]], [[7], [7]]],
 'mode': 'local',
 'retained': [1, 2, 2]}
        actual = handle(request)
        self.assertTrue(equivalent(actual, expected), (actual, expected))

    def test_example_2(self):
        request = {'layer': 5,
 'packets': [{'k': [[0]], 'q': [[0], [0]], 'v': [[2]]},
             {'k': [[0]], 'q': [[0], [0]], 'v': [[10]]}],
 'window': 1}
        expected = {'contexts': [[[2], [2]], [[6], [6]]],
 'mode': 'global',
 'retained': [1, 2]}
        actual = handle(request)
        self.assertTrue(equivalent(actual, expected), (actual, expected))

import unittest
from workload import trial, equivalent


class Part1(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_1_trim_oldest_entry(self):
        args = [[[[[0]], [[1]]], [[[1]], [[2]]]], [[3]], [[4]], 1, 2]
        expected = [[[[1]], [[2]]], [[[3]], [[4]]]]
        actual = trial('retention.append_packet', args)
        self.assertTrue(equivalent(actual, expected), (actual, expected))


class Part2(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_1_contiguous_head_groups_and_different_queries(self):
        args = [[[0], [1], [0], [-1]], [[[[1], [0]], [[3], [7]]], [[[0], [2]], [[2], [9]]]]]
        expected = [[2.5], [2.7310585786300052], [8.0], [7.238405844044234]]
        actual = trial('grouped_read.read', args)
        self.assertTrue(equivalent(actual, expected), (actual, expected))

Compute the KV index using integer division by group size.

stages: Make local cache memory bounded across arrivals while keeping all previous keys and values at global layers.

retention.py · append_packet(entries, keys, values, layer, window) — Return a new chronological list of [keys,values] entries after this token. Global layers retain all, local layers only the newest window. Do not mutate entries.
Implement a separate scaled softmax over retained token positions for each query head. A contiguous group shares keys and values but can produce different contexts.

mission: A text-serving worker must advance a single Gemma 3 attention layer token by token. Five local layers are followed by one global layer. Implement the retention policy and grouped-query read, then verify that head sharing and cache eviction preserve the layer’s causal contexts.
inputs: layer is zero-based and window includes the current token. Each packet supplies projected q [Hq,d], k [Hkv,d] and v [Hkv,dv] for one arriving token. Q/K normalization and rotary position have already been applied upstream. The first packet starts a fresh sequence.
outputs: Return mode ('local' or 'global'), contexts [T,Hq,dv], and retained, the cache length immediately after each packet. Empty input returns empty histories.
constraints: Layers with layer % 6 == 5 use global attention. All others retain the most recent window packets in chronological order. Hq is a positive multiple of Hkv. Contiguous groups of Hq/Hkv query heads share a KV head. Scores use q·k/sqrt(d).
scope: The text decoder’s 5-local/1-global topology, chronological KV eviction and grouped-query attention. This is one layer given projected queries, keys and values. The full multimodal encoder, surrounding residual/MLP stack and training are outside the lab.

source.title: Gemma Team · Gemma 3 Technical Report, section 2

examples.why: Identical zero queries average the retained values. At the third arrival the local window holds only 3 and 11, giving 7.
The sixth layer retains both values despite a local window setting of one. Its second output averages 2 and 10.
